item.title: Evaluating Miami Heat’s Disastrous Start to the 2026-27 Campaign
item.description: Miami Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra reacts against the Dallas Mavericks during the fourth quarter at Kaseya Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Miami Heat is going through a dreadful time. The tough luck that shadowed them last season refuses to leave their side, and, fresh into the new season, the franchise is off to a 0-4 start. A matter of regret and serious self-evaluation for the team and a huge disappointment for the fans. So let’s take a look at what went wrong in those games. Downfall Post the Pre-season The pre-season was a success for the Heat . Out of the five games they played, they won three, with victories over the Toronto Raptors, New Orleans Pelicans, and Brooklyn Nets. They beat the Pelicans (128–118), the Raptors (129–105), and the Brooklyn Nets (144–128). Even their newly acquired superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo had a successful Miami debut, where Erik Spoelstra praised his individual performance. But once the official season began, the situation took a drastic turn. A Look at the First Four Games Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) looks on from the court after the game against the Dallas Mavericks at Kaseya Center. Photo Credit: Sam Navarro, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect So far, the Heat have played four games, and all have been big disappointments. In their season opener against the Minnesota Timberwolves, the Timberwolves remained dominant and took the win 131-106. Antetokounmpo scored a team-high 35 points and grabbed six rebounds against the Timberwolves. Bam Adebayo disappointed with only 15 points, and both Andrew Wiggins and Davion Mitchell scored 11. Minnesota scored 30+ points in each of the four quarters and outscored Miami 65-49 in the second and third quarters. Anthony Edwards recorded 45 points to lead the way for the Timberwolves. Their next clash with the Pistons was also a learning experience, with a 128-111 loss. The weakness of their defense was on full display, and they shot only 15-of-51 (29.4%) from three-point range. Struggling in the first half, the Heat made only 17 of 52 field-goal attempts. Moreover, in the first two quarters, Adebayo and Antetokounmpo were whistled for three fouls. Their third against the Charlotte Hornets was a disaster that has set the internet ablaze. Social media platforms are filled with harsh criticism and allegations, especially after the 115-110 loss to the Hornets, a team fans believed Miami could have easily beaten. The loss also added a sad chapter in the Heat’s history, as it marked the first time they have lost three consecutive games to start the season since 2007-08 and the fifth time ever. There has also been a lack of inspiration, which coach Erik Spoelstra addressed publicly, saying, “I told my team right now that we need inspiration,” and promising they will get there. Though Spoelstra was unhappy about Antetokounmpo fouling out in 25 minutes, he also made it clear that he is not holding them accountable for this loss.

item.description: Marshall Faulk takes powerful stance Parkinson’s diagnosis: ‘This isn’t a death sentence’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Pro Football Hall of Famer and Southern University head football coach Marshall Faulk shocked the football world when he announced his Parkinson’s diagnosis last week, but he’s not allowing the diagnosis to stifle his life. In comments obtained by Brendon Fairbairn, Faulk put the diagnosis into perspective. “What I wanted to do was bring awareness to my fellow brothers: early detection is the best detection. Go get checked, and then, moving forward, continue to focus on coaching and trying to win football games. Because as these things happen a lot of times, what happens is a light gets shined on it, and life stops. That’s not me. I’m always trying to make progress, try to move forward. I’m going to use this to help advocate for other people: hey, man, your life doesn’t have to stop. This isn’t a death sentence. I take medications, and I’m fine. I probably won’t show any symptoms to the naked eye, and I’ll live a full life.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In an appearance on Dr. Sandeep Thakka’s “Caring Neurologist” podcast, Faulk revealed his Parkinson’s diagnosis and said he’d been dealing with symptoms for a year and a half and noticed some of them while he was playing golf. “The rigidity in my hand, just sometimes after I play a lot or I practice a lot,” Faulk said. “I just thought it was normal nerves when putting and stuff like that.” He spoke to his doctor, who pushed him to get checked, and he was diagnosed with Parkinson’s. He described himself as lucky that he was able to catch it early. “Since I’ve started on the medication, I don’t really have a lot of issues,” he said. “I don’t look at it as something that’s terminal. There’s far worse things out there.” He also shared that he hasn’t experienced any decline in his cognitive functions and expressed a desire to help people through his diagnosis. “It’s something you live with,” Faulk said. “I want to help as many people as I can.” Related: Bethune-Cookman’s Raymond Woodie reacts to huge upset over Jackson State Related: Lane College homecoming loss proves that change must come for Fort Valley State

item.title: RFEF fines Barça €602 over Julián Álvarez case
item.description: RFEF fines Barça €602 over Julián Álvarez case The Disciplinary Committee of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has closed the proceedings opened against FC Barcelona following a complaint filed by Atlético de Madrid. The governing body has fined the Catalan club just €602 for breaching the rules when approaching Argentine forward Julián Álvarez. The Atlético board turned to the sporting authorities in late July, believing that Barcelona had made improper contact with the player. Under the General Regulations, any club interested in signing a professional who is under contract must first notify his current club of its intentions in writing. The federation's ruling penalizes Barcelona's conduct under Article 133 of the Disciplinary Code, which concerns failure to comply with regulatory obligations. The offense has been classified as minor, limiting the fine to the maximum amount provided for under that provision. With this ruling, Barça avoids more serious sporting sanctions, such as bans for club officials or partial stadium closures. Atlético has secured official recognition of the breach, but with a merely symbolic penalty. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: One comment from Andoni Iraola today spoke volumes for how he views the Carabao Cup
item.description: One comment from Andoni Iraola today spoke volumes for how he views the Carabao Cup The Carabao Cup can often be regarded as the lowest priority for clubs in the Premier League, at least until the latter rounds after Christmas, but don’t try telling that to Andoni Iraola. Liverpool are in action in that competition on Wednesday night as they host Chelsea at Anfield for a place in the quarter-finals, with the head coach confirming today that he will make a few changes in personnel for the game. It comes amid a hectic period of nine matches in 29 days for the Reds, whose next top-flight fixture on Sunday is a heavyweight home clash against Arsenal, although the Basque is in no mood to treat the Blues’ visit to L4 as an inconvenience. Iraola embracing Carabao Cup ‘opportunity’ In his pre-match press conference on Tuesday lunchtime, Iraola spoke of how he views the Carabao Cup as an ‘opportunity’ to win his first trophy in charge of Liverpool since taking the job in the summer. The 44-year-old said (via liverpoolfc.com ): “I think every competition is an opportunity, especially when you are the coach of Liverpool. You have to take it like this. “I would love to win tomorrow and have the chance to get further in the competition, but I know that we have to play very well. We have to beat a very good team. “It’s also a team that doesn’t play in Europe, so for sure for them this competition is also very important. It’s not going to be easy.” (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Iraola is right not to dismiss the Carabao Cup The Carabao Cup mightn’t seem like Liverpool’s main priority at this stage of the season, but Iraola is respectful of the Reds’ proud heritage in the competition, having won it more often than any other club (10, one ahead of Manchester City). While some might dismiss his comments as mere diplomacy, his phrasing about the tournament being an ‘opportunity’ to win a trophy at Anfield shows that he is indeed prepared to take it seriously. The Basque will make a few line-up changes tomorrow night, for sure, but we don’t see him indulging in the wholesale rotation that Arne Slot implemented at this stage against Crystal Palace last season. Iraola will also know full well that his compatriot and counterpart Xabi Alonso will be especially motivated to win at Anfield, having lost here with Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid in the past two years and then been overlooked for the Liverpool job . The Reds’ campaign won’t be judged on how they perform in the Carabao Cup, but victory on Wednesday would ensure the continuation of winning momentum and a positive mood ahead of the crunch showdown against Arsenal on Sunday. Also, as Iraola recognises, it’s a realistic chance of lifting silverware in his first year in charge on Merseyside.

item.title: Giants finally signing veteran defensive tackle
item.description: Dean Lowry with the Steelers. | Getty Images The New York Giants and veteran defensive tackle Dean Lowry have been linked together for weeks. It appears that Lowry and the Giants are finally coming together, with Dan Duggan of The Athletic reporting that Lowry will join the practice squad. A Giants source confirmed that Lowry is, indeed, signing with the team’s practice squad. Lowry, 32, has played in 132 NFL regular-season games with 85 starts over nine seasons. A fourth-round pick in the 2016 NFL Draft, Lowry spent seven seasons with the Green Bay Packers. He has also spent a year with both the Minnesota Vikings and Pittsburgh Steelers. Lowry, 6-foot-6, 296 pounds, spent last season on IR with the Steelers after tearing his ACL in training camp. The Giants and Lowry were rumored to have mutual interest in early September, but a signing never happened. New York has continued to look for veteran defensive tackle help throughout the season to support D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris. Right now, the Giants have three younger players — Darius Alexander, Bobby Jamison-Travis, and C.J. Okoye — in rotation behind Reader and Harris. Perhaps Lowry can provide some help during the second half of the season.

item.title: IBF orders Shakur Stevenson to face Raymond Muratalla
item.description: After a petition from Top Rank, WBO president Gustavo Olivieri has officially ordered super lightweight champion Shakur Stevenson to face former lightweight titlist Raymond Muratalla, giving the two 20 days to negotiate and avoid a purse bid. It’s a smidge odd that Muratalla (25-0, 17 KO) got the top spot in their 140-pound rankings, as he held the IBF lightweight belt and it’s normally other WBO champions that get this sort of treatment, but it’s hard to argue that other high-rankers like Emiliano Vargas and “Tito” Mercado deserved it more. “Danger” had a damn fine run at 135, beating Tevin Farmer, Zaur Abdullaev, two-time Olympic gold medalist Andy Cruz, and most recently Robson Conceicao. The man can fight and he’s not intimidated by credentials; with unifications and welterweight adventures currently off the table for Stevenson, Muratalla’s probably the most interesting opponent he presently has available to him. Stevenson (25-0, 11 KO) has fought just once this year, cruising past Teofimo Lopez to claim the belt in January. Negotiations with WBA champ Gary Antuanne Russell and welterweight champ Devin Haney fell through, reportedly for financial reasons, and a brief fling with Zuffa Boxing failed to last. He’s short on leverage at the moment and this ruling means that, unless he ditches the belt, Top Rank will get to decide what to pay him for his next outing. I’m sure Bob’s salivating at the chance to show Shakur exactly what he thinks of the latter’s latest shenanigans.

item.description: Photo by Roberto Schmidt/Getty Images Just when you thought sports debates couldn’t get any weirder, Kid Rock decided to throw his name into the WNBA conversation. The WNBA found itself trapped in a headache when former NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White declared for the draft, claiming they identified as women just to expose loopholes in the rulebook. For years, the league skated by on vague wording that simply said players must be women, avoiding any clear-cut medical or biological criteria. But the pair’s trolling finally forced their hand. Commissioner Cathy Engelbert flatly rejected their bids, telling Congress the duo are men and that only women can play, slamming the door on the stunt while dodging the bigger issue. Kid Rock wants to join Enes Kanter in the WNBA Kid Rock and Enes Kanter just couldn’t resist stirring the pot again. In a clip posted online, the pair smirked their way through a stunt claiming they now identify as women and want in on the WNBA draft, turning one of sports’ touchiest debates into their personal comedy routine on X. Enes Kanter: “Hi everyone, once again I identify as a woman. And I cannot wait to be in the WNBA draft in 2027 with my friend.” Kid Rock: “Yep. Me too, I’m a woman also, like, I’m joining.” Kid Rock, born Bob Ritchie, made millions doing what made zero sense on paper: mixing hip-hop, country, and Southern rock into radio anthems like “All Summer Long.” Along the way, his loud, unapologetic style made him a wrestling cult hero, soundtracking pay-per-views and securing him a WWE Hall of Fame ring. item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Robert Gasser Here's the entire list of left-handed pitchers to face the minimum through six innings in a World Series game: Robert Gasser and Sandy Koufax. Going into the postseason, nobody would have believed that Robert Gasser would be by far the best Brewers starting pitcher in the postseason. Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson have been fine, but neither has recorded an out in the sixth inning. Gasser became the first Brewers starter to work more than five innings this postseason, and he did it in dominant fashion. He threw 75 pitches, giving up just one hit and one walk. A pair of double plays kept him from facing any extra batters and gave him some elite company in the record books. Koufax threw two complete games in the 1965 World Series for the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the way things are going right now, it does not look like Gasser will pitch again in this series. Koufax won World Series MVP that year, and it's unlikely Gasser will do the same. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! However, his joining Koufax as the only left-handed pitcher to face the minimum through six innings in a World Series game speaks to how good he was on the biggest stage. He struck out just three batters, but he knew he had an elite defense behind him. Working on 11 days of rest after the Brewers used their best relievers in both Games 1 and 2, Gasser's start set the Brewers up to have all of their best arms ready for their bullpen game on Tuesday. Despite being in the big leagues for a few years, Gasser is still a rookie. He has dealt with some injuries, but this year he has been key to the Brewers' World Series run.
